source: AWS Terrain Tiles (Tilezen/Mapzen terrarium PNG), https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/13/{x}/{y}.png; decoded elevation = R*256 + G + B/256 - 32768 (metres). In this area the underlying dataset is USGS 3DEP/NED (Tilezen source list: https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/data-sources.md)
license/attribution: Terrain Tiles: USGS 3DEP/NED (public domain, U.S. Government); compiled by Mapzen/Tilezen, hosted on AWS Open Data (https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/). Attribution per https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md
projection: local ENU equirectangular, x east m, y north m
projection_detail: x = dlon_rad * N(lat0) * cos(lat0); y = dlat_rad * M(lat0); WGS84 radii at lat0 (M=6359010.6 m, N=6386037.2 m). Grid is the ENU rectangle spanning the bbox edges through the origin.
vertical_datum: As delivered by Terrain Tiles (3DEP is NAVD88, metres); treat as approximate orthometric height. Bay/salt-pond surfaces are encoded near 0 m; values are bare-earth/water-surface, not buildings.
resampling: bilinear in Web-Mercator pixel space of the zoom-13 mosaic
layout: row-major, row 0 = north edge (y = y_max), column 0 = west edge (x = x_min); heights[r*nx + c] at x = x_min + c*dx, y = y_max - r*dy
water_note: water = elevation <= 0.5 m. ASSUMED heuristic: flags Bay, salt ponds and sloughs encoded near sea level; also flags any dry land at <= 0.5 m (levee-protected marsh), so it is an approximate shoreline mask, not a surveyed one.

mission_peak.reference: Mission Peak summit 2,517 ft (767 m), USGS GNIS / https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Peak
